publications.title: Diversification of the BRICS Bloc: From Emerging Global Economies to India’s Autonomy
publications.summary: An examination of BRICS expansion, economic resilience, financial cooperation, digital public infrastructure, sustainability, and India’s pursuit of greater strategic and economic autonomy.
publications.author: Shreya Mahajan

publications.title: The BRICS Transition: Journey From Economic Cooperation Towards Sustainability
publications.summary: A look at BRICS’ evolution from economic cooperation towards climate resilience and sustainable development, highlighting India’s role in advancing a green and inclusive global agenda.
publications.author: Shreya Mahajan

publications.title: The Politics of the Indus
publications.summary: An examination of water, security, and international law in India–Pakistan relations, tracing the Indus Waters Treaty from 1960 to the contemporary dispute over its implementation.
publications.author: Sahana

publications.title: The Politics of Drawing the World
publications.summary: An exploration of how world map projections distort size, shape, distance, and direction, and how cartographic choices influence our understanding of global geography.
publications.author: Sanskar Bajaj

publications.title: When Nature Loses, We Lose Too
publications.summary: A reflection on the importance of SDG 15, the protection of land and biodiversity, and the need to integrate environmental conservation with development and community livelihoods.
publications.author: Sanskar Bajaj

publications.title: Armed But Unstable: Pakistan’s Dangerous Military Path
publications.summary: An analysis of Pakistan’s growing military control, the concentration of authority, and the risks that institutional weakness, political instability, and nuclear posturing pose to regional security.

publications.title: BRICS Summit 2026: India's Leadership & Its Role in West Asia
publications.summary: An overview of the 18th BRICS Summit held in New Delhi, examining India's chairship priorities, economic and technological cooperation, energy security, diplomatic engagement, and the strategic significance of BRICS in the context of West Asia.

publications.title: India–China Border Talks: 36th WMCC Meeting
publications.summary: An overview of the 36th Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination meeting held in New Delhi, focusing on border management, peace and stability along the LAC, and India's approach of combining firm security with sustained diplomatic engagement.

publications.title: India–France Relations: A Stronger Partnership
publications.summary: An examination of India's expanding Special Global Strategic Partnership with France, covering defence, AI and technology, space, innovation, climate action, trade, and cultural cooperation.

publications.title: India's GDP Growth: Strong Growth Despite Global Uncertainty
publications.summary: An economic update on India's Q1 FY2026–27 growth, examining the performance of investment, manufacturing, services, construction, and the digital economy, alongside challenges from agriculture, mining, oil prices, and geopolitical risks.

publications.title: India's Growing Role in Global Politics
publications.summary: An overview of India's evolving geopolitical role amid changing alliances, West Asia tensions, China's growing influence, and the Mecca Pact, highlighting India's multi-alignment strategy and expanding partnerships across regions.

publications.title: India Rejects China's Claims Over Arunachal Pradesh
publications.summary: An analysis of India's decision to identify 27 places in Arunachal Pradesh using standard Indian names on official maps, examining China's renaming campaign and India's position on sovereignty and territorial integrity.

publications.title: Mecca Pact and India's Strategic Response
publications.summary: An overview of the Saudi Arabia–Pakistan–Türkiye collective defence agreement and its implications for India's energy, trade, shipping, regional security, and multi-alignment strategy.

publications.title: The Bankers’ Books Evidence Bill, 2026
publications.summary: Updates banking evidence rules by recognizing digital and cloud records and standardizing certification procedures.

publications.title: The Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026
publications.summary: Proposes more Lok Sabha seats, delimitation based on the 2011 Census, and earlier implementation of women’s reservation.

publications.title: The Income-tax (Amendment) Bill, 2026
publications.summary: Provides tax exemptions for eligible foreign investors in government securities to encourage investment in India’s bond market.

publications.title: The Appropriation (No. 3) Bill, 2026
publications.summary: Seeks Parliament’s approval to regularize excess government expenditure incurred during 2022–23.

publications.title: The Registration of Births and Deaths
publications.summary: Strengthens civil registration through a centralized database, digital certificates, and improved data integration.

publications.title: The Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026
publications.summary: Simplifies corporate compliance, decriminalises minor offences, and proposes changes to governance, CSR, mergers, and corporate regulation.

publications.title: The Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026
publications.summary: Strengthens the 2024 Act with stricter penalties, Special Task Forces, Fast-Track Courts, and time-bound investigations and trials.

publications.title: The Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026
publications.summary: Amends tax laws to address implementation issues, simplify compliance, improve tax administration, and support the digital payments ecosystem.

publications.title: The Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Bill, 2026
publications.summary: Increases the Supreme Court's sanctioned strength from 33 to 37 judges, raising the total strength including the Chief Justice to 38.

publications.title: The Tribunal Reforms Bill, 2026
publications.summary: Proposes an independent National Tribunals Commission to oversee tribunal administration, appointments, infrastructure, and service conditions.

publications.title: The Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Bill, 2026
publications.summary: Extends statutory protection to Vande Mataram and makes intentional disruption of its singing a punishable offence.

publications.title: The Indian Statistical Institute Bill, 2026
publications.summary: Replaces the 1959 Act with a modern framework for ISI, expanding its focus to data science, AI, research, education, and stronger governance.

publications.title: The Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026
publications.summary: Restricts State levies on mineral rights and mineral-bearing land while introducing a more uniform taxation framework for the mining sector.

publications.title: The Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises Development (Amendment) Bill, 2026
publications.summary: Aims to reduce payment delays, simplify compliance, strengthen Udyam registration, and improve online dispute resolution for MSMEs.

publications.title: The National Co-operative Development Corporation (Amendment) Bill, 2026
publications.summary: Enables PACS and cooperative institutions to access loans and financial assistance directly from NCDC, strengthening cooperative financing.

programs.title: Programs
programs.lead: Youth-led programmes designed to create meaningful social impact.
programs.intro: Our programmes focus on empowering young people through participation, leadership and community engagement.

items.title: Khelo India Para Games 2025
items.description: Promoting inclusion, participation and opportunities for young athletes through sport.

details.title: Khelo India Para Games 2025
details.lead: Celebrating sporting excellence, inclusion and the determination of young athletes.
details.participants: Young athletes, volunteers and community members
overview: Youth of Bharat Foundation (YOBHA) took an active initiative to connect KV Gole Market students with the spirit of national-level sports by facilitating their visit to the Indira Gandhi Stadium during the Khelo India Para Games 2025

YOBHA created an opportunity for students to engage in activities, participate in games, and experience the energy and inclusivity of a major sporting event. The initiative helped students develop greater interest in sports while promoting fitness, confidence, teamwork, and an appreciation for para-athletes and inclusive sporting excellence.

Through this initiative, YOBHA demonstrated its commitment to providing young people with meaningful exposure, opportunities, and experiences beyond the classroom, inspiring them to participate, explore their potential, and contribute to a stronger and more active India.

items.title: Hindu Nav Varsh Mahotsav 2025
items.description: Celebrating India's cultural heritage while bringing young people together.

details.title: Hindu Nav Varsh Mahotsav 2025
details.lead: Celebrating culture, heritage and youth participation.
overview: Youth of Bharat Foundation (YOBHA) organised and facilitated the Hindu Nav Varsh Mahotsav 2025 at Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU), Delhi, creating a dedicated platform for young people to celebrate India’s cultural heritage and civilisational values.

YOBHA brought together students and youth through cultural performances, interactive activities, and inspiring conversations, encouraging meaningful participation in the celebration of Hindu Nav Varsh. The initiative was designed to strengthen young people’s connection with Sanatan Sanskriti, Indian traditions, and cultural identity.

Through the Mahotsav, YOBHA demonstrated its commitment to youth-led cultural engagement, providing young Indians with opportunities to celebrate, learn, participate, and take ownership of India’s rich heritage.

items.title: Civil Defence Volunteer Registration Drive
items.description: Mobilising young people for civic participation, community safety and disaster preparedness.

details.title: Civil Defence Volunteer Registration Drive
details.lead: Empowering youth to contribute to community safety, emergency preparedness and nation-building.
details.location: Miranda House, University of Delhi, New Delhi
overview: Youth of Bharat Foundation (YOBHA), in collaboration with the Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports, engaged students at Miranda House, University of Delhi, through a dedicated Civil Defence Volunteer registration initiative.

YOBHA's team mobilised students, facilitated registrations, guided participants through the enrolment process, and encouraged young people to take responsibility for national service and disaster preparedness.

The initiative transformed student enthusiasm into meaningful civic participation, creating opportunities for youth to contribute to community safety, emergency response, resilience, and nation-building.
Through such on-ground interventions, YOBHA continues to connect young Indians with opportunities to serve their communities and strengthen the nation.

items.title: International Yoga Day 2025
items.description: Promoting yoga, fitness and mindful living among young students through active participation.

details.title: International Yoga Day 2025
details.lead: Promoting fitness, discipline, mindfulness and holistic well-being among young people.
details.location: KV Gole Market, New Delhi, India
overview: On 21 June 2025, Youth of Bharat Foundation (YOBHA) engaged with the students of KV Gole Market to mark International Yoga Day 2025, creating an opportunity for young students to experience the benefits of yoga, fitness, and mindful living.
YOBHA facilitated student participation, encouraged regular physical activity, and promoted yoga as a means of building discipline, focus, strength, and overall well-being.
The students demonstrated various yoga practices, bringing energy and enthusiasm to the celebration while highlighting the importance of maintaining a healthy and balanced lifestyle.

Through this initiative, YOBHA strengthened its commitment to youth fitness and holistic development, inspiring young Indians to embrace healthier lifestyles and the values of balance, discipline, and unity.

items.title: Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat @2047
items.description: Mobilising youth for a healthy, empowered and drug-free India through awareness, fitness and community action.

details.title: Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat @2047
details.lead: Building awareness, promoting fitness and empowering young people to contribute to a drug-free Bharat.
details.participants: Youth representatives, volunteers and community participants
overview: Youth of Bharat Foundation (YOBHA) actively participated in the Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat @2047 Youth Spiritual Summit held in Varanasi from 18 to 20 July 2025, joining a national movement focused on building a healthy, conscious, empowered and drug-free youth population.

The three-day programme, organised under the Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports through MY Bharat, brought together young representatives from spiritual, socio-cultural and youth organisations at the Rudraksh International Cooperation and Convention Centre. The summit focused on understanding addiction, strengthening youth-led outreach, and developing a roadmap towards a drug-free India by 2047.

YOBHA's team actively contributed to the campaign through youth mobilisation, awareness-building and participation in the anti-drug movement. The team engaged with young leaders, volunteers and organisations working towards a Nasha Mukt Bharat and strengthened collective efforts for youth empowerment.

As part of the campaign, the YOBHA team participated in the Fit India Sundays on Cycle initiative at Banaras Hindu University (BHU) on 20 July. The cycling drive connected the message of a drug-free India with fitness, discipline and purposeful living.

During the Varanasi visit, the YOBHA team also visited the Banaras Hindu University campus, interacted with students and volunteers, and connected with the campus youth ecosystem. These engagements created opportunities for dialogue around student issues, youth-led initiatives and community action.

The programme concluded with the adoption of the Kashi Declaration, a youth-led framework calling for coordinated action involving spiritual organisations, educational institutions, government bodies and civil society to strengthen prevention, awareness, rehabilitation and community mobilisation against substance abuse.

Through its participation in the Varanasi initiative, YOBHA strengthened its engagement with national youth programmes, promoted fitness and awareness, and contributed to the broader mission of building a Nasha Mukt Bharat.

items.title: Bihar Food Drive
items.description: Spreading smiles and supporting families in need through grassroots food distribution.

details.title: Bihar Food Drive
details.lead: Spreading smiles and strengthening communities through compassion and grassroots service.
details.participants: Local families, community members and YOBHA volunteers
overview: On 14 May 2025, Youth of Bharat Foundation (YOBHA) organised a food distribution drive in Bawangama, Sitamarhi, Bihar, reaching out to families and individuals in need.

YOBHA's team and volunteers came together to distribute meals and extend support to the local community. The initiative focused not only on providing nourishment but also on strengthening the spirit of compassion and community service.

The food drive reflected YOBHA's commitment to grassroots engagement and meaningful community action, demonstrating how collective efforts can provide immediate support to people facing difficult circumstances.
Through this initiative, YOBHA reinforced its belief that meaningful change begins at the community level by standing with those in need and turning small acts of service into lasting social impact.

items.title: International Youth Day 2025: Local Youth Actions for the SDGs and Beyond
items.description: Empowering young leaders to connect grassroots action with the Sustainable Development Goals and inclusive community development.

details.title: International Youth Day 2025: Local Youth Actions for the SDGs and Beyond
details.lead: Connecting local youth action with the Sustainable Development Goals and building responsible community leaders.
details.location: MY Bharat Meeting Hall, Ananthapur, Andhra Pradesh, India
details.participants: Young leaders, educators, government representatives, youth workers and experts
overview: Youth of Bharat Foundation (YOBHA), in collaboration with MY Bharat Ananthapur, Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports, and Pragathi Padham Youth Association, organised a vibrant celebration of International Youth Day 2025 at the MY Bharat Meeting Hall, Ananthapur.

Built around the theme 'Local Youth Actions for the SDGs and Beyond,' the programme brought together young leaders, educators, government representatives, youth workers, and experts for meaningful dialogue on youth-led action and sustainable development.

YOBHA actively contributed by bringing together youth stakeholders, facilitating participation, supporting the programme, and creating a platform for young leaders to share ideas, local solutions, and perspectives on achieving the Sustainable Development Goals.
The programme also recognised participating young leaders through Certificates of Recognition, acknowledging their contribution and commitment to youth-led development and community action.

Through this initiative, YOBHA strengthened its commitment to empowering young people, connecting grassroots action with national and global development goals, and building a generation of responsible, engaged, and impact-oriented youth leaders.

items.title: International Youth Day 2025: Local Youth Actions for the SDGs and Beyond
items.description: Mobilising young people to turn the Sustainable Development Goals into meaningful grassroots action.

details.title: International Youth Day 2025: Local Youth Actions for the SDGs and Beyond
details.lead: Mobilising young leaders to transform local challenges into meaningful action for sustainable development.
details.participants: Young leaders, changemakers and community representatives
overview: Youth of Bharat Foundation (YOBHA), in collaboration with MY Bharat Nagarkurnool, Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports, UN Volunteers India, and Swami Vivekananda Seva Brundam, organised and facilitated an International Youth Day 2025 celebration in Kalwakurthy, Telangana.

Built around the theme 'Local Youth Actions for the SDGs and Beyond,' the programme brought together young leaders, changemakers, and community representatives to discuss how locally driven youth initiatives can contribute to the Sustainable Development Goals and broader development priorities.
YOBHA played an active role in mobilising young participants, coordinating with partner organisations, facilitating youth engagement, and creating a platform for dialogue and exchange.

Interactive sessions encouraged participants to identify local challenges, share ideas, and explore practical ways to translate the SDGs into grassroots action. Participants were also recognised through Certificates of Recognition for their contribution to youth-led development initiatives.

Through the Kalwakurthy celebration, YOBHA strengthened its grassroots youth network and demonstrated its commitment to connecting young people with national and international development frameworks while turning youth participation into meaningful community action.

items.title: Independence Day Celebration 2025: Celebrating the Spirit of Bharat
items.description: Engaging students in celebrating India's freedom, unity, civic responsibility and national progress.

details.title: Independence Day Celebration 2025: Celebrating the Spirit of Bharat
details.lead: Inspiring young students to connect with the values of freedom, patriotism, civic responsibility and nation-building.
details.location: KV Gole Market, New Delhi, India
overview: Youth of Bharat Foundation (YOBHA), in collaboration with KV Gole Market, organised a special Independence Day celebration to engage students in commemorating India's journey of freedom, unity, and national progress.
YOBHA facilitated student participation, coordinated the programme, and created a platform for young students to connect with the values of patriotism, civic responsibility, and nation-building.
The celebration encouraged students to remember the sacrifices of India's freedom fighters while reflecting on their own role in shaping the nation's future.

The initiative reinforced YOBHA's commitment to connecting youth with national occasions through meaningful engagement and educational experiences, inspiring the next generation to contribute towards a stronger, united, and progressive Bharat.

items.title: YOBHA–MyGov India: Strengthening Youth Outreach & Digital Engagement
items.description: Strengthening institutional partnerships and creating new opportunities for youth participation through digital and campus engagement.

details.title: YOBHA–MyGov India: Strengthening Youth Outreach & Digital Engagement
details.lead: Building stronger government–youth connections through campus outreach, digital participation and strategic collaboration.
details.location: MyGov India Office, New Delhi, India
overview: A delegation from the Youth of Bharat Foundation (YOBHA) visited the MyGov India office in New Delhi for a strategic discussion focused on strengthening youth outreach, digital engagement, and awareness of government initiatives.

YOBHA representatives engaged with the MyGov outreach and creative teams to explore opportunities for expanding youth participation through platforms such as MyGov Campus, Campus Content Creators, and MyGov Campus Societies.

YOBHA presented its vision for connecting young people with Union Government flagship programmes, strengthening awareness at campus and grassroots levels, and encouraging youth to become active participants in governance and nation-building.
The meeting opened avenues for potential collaboration around youth mobilisation, campus engagement, digital storytelling, content creation, and dissemination of public initiatives.
The engagement marked an important step towards building stronger institutional linkages and developing innovative platforms through which India's youth can participate in national development.

projects.title: Projects
projects.lead: Time-bound pieces of work with a defined research question, a field component and a published output.
projects.intro: Projects typically run six to eighteen months. Each begins with a scoping note and ends with a published report; interim findings are tested in closed roundtables before release.

campaigns.title: Campaigns
campaigns.lead: Public campaigns that carry research findings into communities, delivered with district administrations and partner institutions.
campaigns.intro: Campaigns are the Foundation's public-facing arm. Each is grounded in a published finding and delivered through the volunteer corps in partnership with local administration.

events.title: Events
events.lead: Roundtables, seminars and the annual Bharat Series — most open to students by registration.
events.intro: The Foundation convenes throughout the year. Registration details are published four weeks in advance and reserved seats are held for students at every convening.

training.title: Training
training.lead: Structured training in research method, policy writing and data analysis for students, volunteers and partner staff.
training.intro: Training is delivered as short intensive modules, both in person and online. Modules are open to volunteers, partner institution staff and students on request.

awareness-drives.title: Awareness Drives
awareness-drives.lead: Short, focused community drives run by the volunteer corps on issues our research has identified as underserved.
awareness-drives.intro: Drives run for one to four weeks in a defined geography. Each is designed around a specific behaviour or entitlement, with outcomes recorded and reported.

relief-operations.title: Relief Operations
relief-operations.lead: Coordinated volunteer response during disasters and emergencies, always under the direction of local authorities.
relief-operations.intro: The Foundation does not lead relief operations. We mobilise trained volunteers in support of district administration and established relief agencies, and we publish an account of every deployment.

upcomingEvents.title: Khelo India Para Games Roundtable 2026
upcomingEvents.description: A closed-door roundtable on para-sport infrastructure, athlete pathways and the policy architecture supporting adaptive sport in India.

upcomingEvents.title: Seminar on the Union Budget 2026
upcomingEvents.description: Narasimha Murthy leads a working seminar on the fiscal framing of the Union Budget and its implications for youth employment.

upcomingEvents.title: Bharat Series: Annual Policy Dialogue
upcomingEvents.description: Our flagship day-long dialogue, convened with Hindu College at the Caucus Sanganeria Auditorium, bringing together scholars and practitioners.

pastEvents.title: Campus Policy Dialogue Series
pastEvents.summary: A travelling dialogue series taking policy questions directly to undergraduate campuses.

pastEvents.title: Nasha Mukt Yuva Abhiyan
pastEvents.summary: A youth-led awareness campaign on substance abuse, delivered with district administrations.

pastEvents.title: Bharat Youth Urban Dialogue
pastEvents.summary: An urban governance convening on municipal finance and city-level service delivery.

pastEvents.title: National Volunteer Summit
pastEvents.summary: Bringing together volunteer coordinators from across the Foundation's state chapters.

podcast.title: The Bharat Policy Conversation
podcast.lead: Long-form conversations with researchers, administrators and practitioners about the decisions shaping India's next decade.
podcast.intro: New episodes every second Thursday. Each runs forty to sixty minutes, is recorded unedited except for length, and is accompanied by a reading list drawn from our own archive.

episodes.title: What district administration actually does
episodes.summary: The gap between how policy is written in Delhi and how it lands in a district of four million people — staffing, budgets and the limits of the collector's office.

episodes.title: Learning outcomes and the measurement problem
episodes.summary: Why national assessments and classroom reality diverge, and what a more honest measurement regime would look like.

episodes.title: The unicorn decade, reviewed
episodes.summary: A hundred unicorns later — what the start-up boom did for employment, and what it did not.

episodes.title: Para-sport and the infrastructure question
episodes.summary: Athlete pathways, accessible facilities and the policy architecture that either supports or blocks them.

episodes.title: Two point four billion dollars, thrown away
episodes.summary: Cold chains, storage and the post-harvest losses India absorbs every year without much public argument.

episodes.title: Reading a Union Budget properly
episodes.summary: How to look past the headline numbers to the allocations that actually determine youth outcomes.

board-of-trustees.title: Board of Trustees
board-of-trustees.lead: The Board holds fiduciary responsibility for the Foundation, approves the annual budget and appoints the executive leadership.
board-of-trustees.intro: Trustees are appointed for a three-year term and meet quarterly. The Board does not direct research findings; its remit is financial stewardship, statutory compliance and the appointment of the executive.

governing-council.title: Governing Council
governing-council.lead: The Council sets the research agenda each financial year and reviews published output against the Foundation's mandate.
governing-council.intro: Council members are drawn from academia, public administration and civil society. They meet twice a year and their review notes are summarised in the annual review.

president.title: President
president.lead: The President sets the Foundation's research agenda and represents it before government, academic and international partners.

profiles.name: NAME OF PRESIDENT
biography: The President is the Foundation's principal representative and chairs the internal research committee. The office is responsible for the intellectual direction of the Foundation's five verticals and for its relationships with government, universities and international partners.
The President serves a five-year term, appointed by the Board of Trustees, and reports to the Governing Council on the Foundation's published output each financial year.
responsibilities: Sets the annual research agenda with the Governing Council
Chairs the internal review committee for all publications
Represents the Foundation before government and international partners
Appoints Distinguished Fellows on the Council's recommendation

executive-vice-president.title: Executive Vice Presidents
executive-vice-president.lead: The Executive Vice President oversees programme delivery, institutional partnerships and the Foundation's state chapters.

profiles.name: NAME OF EXECUTIVE VICE PRESIDENT
biography: The Executive Vice President carries operational responsibility for programme delivery, field campaigns, convenings and the network of state chapters.
The office also manages institutional partnerships, from university collaborations to memoranda with government departments.
responsibilities: Directs programme and field campaign delivery across states
Manages institutional partnerships and collaboration agreements
Oversees the volunteer corps and state chapter network
Reports on programme outcomes to the Board each quarter

director.title: Directors
director.lead: The Directors lead the Foundation's research, programmes and institutional functions across different areas of work.

profiles.name: CHANDAN MATCHA
biography: The Director runs the research desk day to day: commissioning work, supervising fellows, and holding every draft to the Foundation's published method before it goes to advisory review.
The office is also responsible for research ethics, data governance and the open-publication commitment.
responsibilities: Commissions and supervises all research projects
Mentors the research fellowship cohort
Enforces research ethics and data governance standards
Prepares the research section of the annual review

profiles.name: JAMPANA RANGA RAJU
biography: The Director of Programmes oversees the planning and implementation of the Foundation's programmes and youth engagement initiatives.
The office coordinates programme teams and ensures that projects remain aligned with the Foundation's mission and institutional objectives.
responsibilities: Leads programme planning and implementation
Coordinates programme teams
Monitors programme outcomes
Develops new youth engagement initiatives

profiles.name: VIKRAM THAKUR
biography: The Operations Head oversees the organisation’s day-to-day operations and ensures that internal processes, programmes and teams function efficiently. The office supports effective coordination, operational planning and smooth execution of organisational activities.
The office supports long-term collaboration and institutional engagement.
responsibilities: Oversees day-to-day organisational operations
Coordinates internal teams and workflows
Supports programme and event execution
Ensures efficient administrative processes
Monitors operational planning and implementation

distinguished-fellows.title: Distinguished Fellows
distinguished-fellows.lead: Senior scholars and former practitioners who anchor a research vertical and mentor the cohort within it.
distinguished-fellows.intro: Distinguished Fellows are appointed by the President on the recommendation of the Governing Council. Each anchors one vertical, reviews its output and supervises the research fellows working within it.

research-fellows.title: Research Fellows
research-fellows.lead: Full-time researchers appointed for a two-year term, each responsible for a defined line of enquiry.
research-fellows.intro: Research Fellows publish under their own name. The fellowship is a salaried, full-time appointment and is open to graduates nationwide through an annual application round.

visiting-fellows.title: Visiting Fellows
visiting-fellows.lead: Academics and practitioners in residence for a fixed period, contributing to a specific project or convening.
visiting-fellows.intro: Visiting Fellowships run from three to twelve months. Fellows retain their primary affiliation and contribute to one named project, usually culminating in a joint publication or convening.

centres.title: Centres
centres.lead: Specialist units within the Foundation, each with a standing research programme and its own convening calendar.
body: The Foundation organises its longer-running work into centres. A centre differs from a vertical in that it carries its own convening calendar, maintains standing relationships with a specific set of institutions, and often hosts visiting fellows for the duration of a project.
Centres publish under the Foundation's imprint and are subject to the same review process as any other output.

cards.title: Centre for Parliamentary Studies
cards.description: Legislative analysis and briefing material prepared for members of Parliament, state legislators and their research staff.

cards.title: Centre for Education Policy
cards.description: Implementation research on the National Education Policy, learning outcomes and the education-to-employment transition.

cards.title: Centre for Economic Enquiry
cards.description: Enterprise, formalisation, agricultural value chains and the fiscal choices behind India's growth path.

cards.title: Centre for Public Health Systems
cards.description: District health infrastructure, out-of-pocket expenditure and programme evaluation.

cards.title: Centre for Sustainability
cards.description: Climate commitments, clean energy transition and the urban waste economy.

cards.title: Centre for Youth & Civic Life
cards.description: Youth participation in public life, volunteering, sport and civic education.

site.name: Youth of Bharat Foundation
site.tagline: A youth-led public policy research foundation
site.description: An independent, non-partisan foundation advancing evidence-based public policy research and building the next generation of India's civic leadership.

contact.address: B5/57, Humayunpur Road, Safdarjung Enclave, New Delhi 110029

values.title: Non-partisan by constitution
values.description: The Foundation takes no party position. Our research is evaluated on method and evidence, never on political convenience.

values.title: Open by default
values.description: Every report, brief and dataset we produce is published in full and made freely available to the public.

values.title: Rigorous over rapid
values.description: We publish when a finding survives review. Peer scrutiny and advisory review precede every release.

values.title: Young people as authors
values.description: Research is led by fellows in their twenties, supervised by senior practitioners. Authorship is credited, not absorbed.
